You got into your dream college. But the machine that keeps you breathing weighs eight hundred pounds.
Ed Roberts got polio at fourteen. It paralyzed him from the neck down, and he slept in an iron lung.
The state said he was too disabled to ever hold a job. And the university said no dorm could take him.
You're Ed. Three options. Which one would you pick?
Take the university to court, and make it give you a room.
Study from home, and take your classes by telephone.
Move into the campus hospital, and call it your dorm.
Option A sounds right. But in nineteen sixty-two, there was no law to sue under. The first federal one came eleven years later.
Option B sounds easy. But that's how he did high school, by telephone, from his bedroom. He wanted to be in the room.
Option C is what he did. The head of campus health offered an empty hospital wing. Ed said yes, on one condition. Treat it as a dorm, not a ward.
More disabled students followed. They called themselves the Rolling Quads.
And in nineteen seventy-six, the state that said he couldn't hold a job made him director of that same agency.
Today, the A.D.A. says a curb ramp can rise one inch for every twelve, at most.
Level cleared. Comment what you picked, and follow for level three.
